q: how big is a eurasian lynx
a: The Eurasian lynx (Lynx lynx) is the largest wild cat in Europe and the third-largest predator on the continent after the brown bear and gray wolf. It is recognizable by its long black ear tufts, distinctive facial ruff, short bobbed tail with a black tip, and large paws that function like snowshoes in deep winter snow. Adult males weigh 18-30 kg (40-66 lb) and females slightly less. The Eurasian lynx is a solitary ambush hunter that preys mainly on roe deer, and also takes hares, birds, and occasionally reindeer calves; a single lynx may kill 50-70 roe deer per year. Its range spans Scandinavia, the Baltics, the Carpathians, the Balkans, and eastward through Russia to the Pacific. Sweden hosts a thriving population of roughly 1,400-2,000 lynx in its northern and central forests, while Poland's population of around 200-300 animals is concentrated in the Białowieża Forest, Carpathians, and Bieszczady Mountains. The lynx was hunted to near extinction in much of Western Europe by the 19th century, and reintroduction programs in Switzerland, France, Germany, and the Czech Republic have had mixed success.
